steps.what: Patrol trails, slopes or swimming areas to observe conditions and participants
Monitor swimmers or other participants from the assigned observation position

tasks.design: Retain direct patrol and monitoring. Actual condition and incident recording is separately designed in 5045 using the incident records system {OTHER}; no sensor or camera deployment is presumed to remove observation time.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work requires a person who can recognise danger and respond in the actual area.
tasks.enabler_now: No identified component removes this observation work while preserving the response boundary.
tasks.still_hard: Visibility, changing conditions and ambiguous distress demand continuous attention.
tasks.human_edge: The worker recognises an unsafe situation and can immediately intervene.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in patrol coverage, observation time or responsibility.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of protective service workers

evidence.claim: Direct recreational safety observation is situated work; no labour substitution is established by the supplied digest. This is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is actual movement and direct observation. Emergency contact is explicitly present in 5040, warnings in 5044, and real condition/incident first capture in 5045. Those actions are not hidden inside the patrol steps or credited twice.

The assigned area comes from the existing duty allocation and the worker observes the actual environment; no structured sensor input is assumed. Any unclear coverage is clarified within retained work.

Before assigning zero, separate actual records and communications: first condition and incident entry is s2 of 5045 and its original observation is s1 of that task. If local timing combines the same observation with patrol, roll-up must assign that action one owner, not add a duplicate saving.
No routine patrol log, report or broadcast is invented. No new tool is deployed for patrol itself, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Actual patrol and stationary monitoring pattern
Whether a separate routine patrol log is genuinely kept
research_questions: Is there any actual record write or send inside local patrol duties beyond the separately listed tasks?

incremental.description: No added patrol tool or configuration

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All one hundred patrol and observation hours remain. Actual recording and emergency contact are explicitly separated; no changed physical or informational step remains within this boundary.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Contact emergency medical personnel for serious injury

steps.what: Recognise serious injury and establish the need for emergency medical personnel
Confirm exact location, access route and emergency contact channel
Initiate the emergency call on the confirmed phone or radio channel
Describe injury, location and access and answer the dispatcher's questions
Receive instructions and communicate material changes during the emergency call

tasks.design: Use the existing direct emergency phone or radio procedure without an added software intermediary. Keep the contact action separate from the live dispatch conversation; any later incident entry belongs in the incident records system {OTHER} under 5045.
tasks.previous_blocker: The caller must communicate rapidly changing facts and answer questions in real time.
tasks.enabler_now: The current direct contact method already reaches the emergency channel; no additional automation is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Uncertain location, changing injury and access constraints require immediate human clarification.
tasks.human_edge: The worker sees the scene, answers precisely and acts on instructions.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in emergency contact time or authority.

reach.learn: Location, access and factual injury description

evidence.claim: A direct emergency call involves scene judgement and live clarification; no saving from adding automation is established here. This is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is requesting emergency medical help, not treating the injury. Later treatment and incident documentation is explicitly captured in 5045, not treated as free or removed.

The worker supplies observed condition and verified location in s1-s2; the existing emergency instructions supply the phone number or radio channel. No automatic location feed, generated triage or prewritten clean incident record is assumed.

The real contact initiation is separately priced at five hours and remains fully retained. The immediate worker decision in s2 binds that channel and scene; it adds no remote approval delay. A changed location or channel requires confirmation again.

Checked the actual send/call separately before assigning zero: existing direct dialing or radio contact already performs it. No same-system save or report generation is claimed, and no tool is deployed, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Local emergency contact and location procedure
research_questions: Does the current contact procedure contain any duplicate dispatch entry rather than direct calling?

approvals.approved_version: s2 confirmed incident location, access route and exact emergency phone or radio channel for this immediate call; changes require reconfirmation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All one hundred hours remain, including the separately identified real contact initiation. No duplicate entry, intermediary send or document assembly has been identified to remove.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Warn participants about unsafe conditions or conduct

steps.what: Verify inclement weather, unsafe areas or illegal conduct affecting participants
Choose the warning, affected area and necessary participant action
Warn participants verbally and explain the required safe behaviour
Observe understanding and respond to questions or continued unsafe behaviour
Display the selected existing warning flag or sign for the affected area

tasks.design: Retain verification, direct warnings and physical warning signs under the current protocol. Use current weather information already available through the weather service {OTHER}; no automated public broadcast or generated warning is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: A warning must fit actual conditions and the participants' response.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing direct warnings and standard signs already express the necessary message without composition software.
tasks.still_hard: People may misunderstand, disagree or continue unsafe conduct.
tasks.human_edge: The worker adapts tone, checks understanding and intervenes when a warning is insufficient.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in warning work or authority.

evidence.claim: Direct safety warnings and physical standard signs require situational judgement; these retained-work estimates are model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes the actual spoken warning and, in an area using them today, display of an existing standard warning sign or flag. No new notice-writing or compliance log is invented.

The worker supplies actual condition and conduct observations; existing weather information supplies time and forecast. Verification and message selection remain in s1-s2, with manual clarification for stale or missing weather data.

The physical public warning is a separately priced action. The worker's immediate s2 decision binds the exact existing sign, area and conditions; if the intervening discussion reveals a change, repeat that decision before display. No remote approval delay or new warning artefact is required.

Checked records, reports and sends before assigning zero: actual condition and incident entry is priced in 5045; this warning branch has no separate written message to generate. All current work remains and no new tool needs upkeep.
unknowns: Whether this recreational area uses standard flags or signs
Any existing electronic broadcast work actually performed
research_questions: Is there an actual repetitive written broadcast separate from these direct warnings?

approvals.approved_version: s2 selected existing warning sign or flag, exact area, current conditions and required action; changed conditions void this decision

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All one hundred hours remain. The actual physical warning action is separately priced and unchanged, and no additional record or broadcast baseline is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain condition, treatment and incident records

steps.what: Establish actual beach conditions, treatment facts and incident details
First enter condition, treatment and incident facts in the incident records system {OTHER}
Enter site, recorder and record-date headers
Copy current reported weather readings into the actual condition record
Verify exact treatment, chronology, local conditions and weather-source applicability
Save the condition and incident record in the same system

tasks.design: Configure record-context defaults and a native import of existing reported weather values into the incident records system {OTHER}. Keep all first capture of local conditions, treatment and incidents and all semantic checking with the worker; imported station readings never replace local observation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated headers and copying weather readings can be mixed with sensitive first-hand incident documentation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native defaults and a source-tagged weather import can address exact repetition without generating treatment facts.
tasks.still_hard: A nearby weather station may not describe the beach, and treatment chronology must be exact.
tasks.human_edge: The worker knows what happened, what care was given and which details remain uncertain.
tasks.altitude: Less repeat weather copying if a compatible source exists; first-hand incident responsibility is unchanged.

reach.learn: Precise time, action and uncertainty recording

evidence.claim: Native record defaults and transfer of existing weather values are plausible deterministic components; the role-specific workflow and timings are model knowledge, not supported by the unrelated investigation cases in the digest.

assumptions: Boundary is the actual condition, medical treatment and incident record required by this task. It explicitly contains first factual entry; patrol and emergency-contact tasks do not claim that entry again. If the original observation in s1 is the same action as patrol monitoring, roll-up must assign it one owner.

The worker supplies observed beach conditions, treatment, times, incident narrative and uncertainties in fully retained s1-s2. Existing weather service readings supply station ID, observation time, parameter, value, unit and quality flag; absent or inapplicable readings require manual recording, not an invented feed.

Of ten header hours, only one is repeated current site, author and date entry; nine remain for actual event identifiers, time corrections and checks. Fifteen weather-copy hours concern values already read from a separate source today, not a same-system save or sensor runtime.

Native defaults and import are tested before custom code. All nineteen verification hours remain. The one-hour ordinary author save stays retained and ungated; no new report, disclosure or emergency notification is created.
unknowns: Actual weather source and station coverage
Whether weather values are presently copied at all
Current form defaults and sensitive record access
research_questions: Can imported values retain station provenance and remain clearly distinct from observed local beach conditions?

already_counted.description: Check treatment meaning, event chronology and weather applicability

incremental.description: Maintain record defaults and weather mapping and handle source failures

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross is one header hour plus fifteen actual weather-copy hours, less two upkeep = 14. Cautious case: the station fails local applicability checks and all fifteen weather hours remain manual; one header hour is still removed but two upkeep hours persist while the mapping is checked, giving minus one. Treatment capture and ordinary saving never shrink.

skills_to_grow: Check weather provenance and local applicability
